text: What happened to Lions linebacker Jack Campbell?
He went down on a tackle Sunday and didn't move.
Here's what a hit to the neck can do.
Your neck is seven small bones stacked around your spinal cord.
That cord carries every signal between your brain and your body.
Bend the neck too far and the bones can pinch the cord.
Signals below that spot slow down or stop. Arms and legs can go numb or weak.
That's why trainers hold the head still and strap the player to a hard board.
A milder hit can stun the cord. It wakes back up in minutes or hours.
A harder hit can bruise it. It swells and heals over days or weeks as the swelling goes down.
His team hasn't said what his injury is.
But on Wednesday he said he has full movement in his lower body and his upper body is getting better.
